basis: Vascular tumor with platelet trapping and consumptive coagulopathy; purpura is a bleeding sign; hepatic hemangiomas are occasional.
Limb defects, ectodermal dysplasia and orofacial clefting define EEC; ocular, renal and hearing defects lack established >=30% frequency in this subtype.
Renal cystic dysplasia, diabetes and neurodevelopmental impairment are the defining manifestations; other structural abnormalities are occasional.
Congenital cardiac shunting with pulmonary arterial vascular disease; pulmonary hypertension belongs to the cardiovascular axis.
Congenital absence or complete cleft of the sternum; associated heart abnormalities and breathing symptoms are not defining organ damage.
Skeletal dysplasia with delayed epiphyseal and carpal ossification and characteristic hand-bone abnormalities.
Malignant tumor involving the cauda equina nerve roots.
Displacement of the carpal bones is a structural musculoskeletal disorder; no additional organ involvement is established.
Thymic neuroendocrine carcinoma is an endocrine-cell neoplasm; no common additional organ damage or hormone syndrome is established.
Long QT, syndactyly and neurodevelopmental abnormalities define disease; microdontia 17/17 supports dental involvement. Metabolic abnormalities in ~35-40% omitted under cap.
Adrenal chromaffin tumor; direct catecholamine-mediated hypertension occurs in ~80-90%. Cardiomyopathy, stroke and retinopathy are minority complications.
Failure of eyelid closure is an eyelid disorder; associated corneal injury remains within the ocular axis.
Inherited macular retinal degeneration with photoreceptor and pigment epithelial loss; hypertension in one reported patient does not establish disease-related vascular damage.
Leucine-metabolism disorder; neurologic movement impairment is annotated frequent (30-79%); expressivity ranges to asymptomatic adults.
GATA5-related congenital structural heart disease; the reported manifestations are confined to the cardiovascular axis.
Cerebral and retinal microangiopathy define disease; gastrointestinal hemorrhage occurs in 1/2 reported patients. Recurrent fractures in 1/2 omitted under the four-axis cap.
Palmoplantar keratoderma and motor/sensory neuropathy define disease; fixed pes cavus occurs in 80-99%, supporting musculoskeletal involvement.
Brain malformations and developmental disability with characteristic coloboma/ptosis; hearing and cardiac defects lack established >=30% frequency for this ACTB subtype.
SCN1B-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; seizures, developmental impairment and motor signs reflect nervous-system dysfunction.
Endothelial vascular neoplasm commonly occupies dermis/subcutis and skeletal muscle, each in roughly half or more of patients; bone involvement alone is less common.
COL2A1 disorders primarily affect cartilage and skeleton; vitreoretinal abnormalities and myopia are common (>30%) across major phenotypes. Hearing involvement varies by subtype.
Retinal cone-rod degeneration and hearing loss jointly define the syndrome.
Congenital neutropenia with impaired host defense; recurrent gingival inflammation affects 4/4 reported patients. Cutaneous warts are not established for this subtype.
Intrinsic cerebral small-vessel fragility with hemorrhagic and white-matter brain injury defines the disorder.
Benign nipple duct neoplasm arising in breast tissue, outside the axes; overlying focal epidermal erosion does not establish a separate dermatologic disease.
